newsitem.title: TURKEY: U.S. group says Turkish rights lawyers harassed.
newsitem.headline: U.S. group says Turkish rights lawyers harassed.

text.p: A U.S.-based human rights group said in a report released on Thursday that Turkish authorities often prosecuted and threatened lawyers who tried to focus foreign attention on rights abuses in Turkey.

"A striking feature of our conversations with lawyers was the frequency with which they complained of being threatened or punished for communicating human rights information to international bodies," the report by the Lawyers Committee for Human Rights.
The group also said Turkish lawyers were pressured into not defending suspects accused of involvement in Kurdish and left-wing militant activity.
"Either you are threatened or bribed to get rid of you," the report quoted Senal Sarihan, head of Turkey's Contemporary Lawyers' Association, as saying of official pressure on lawyers.

Turkey is under strong European legal and political pressure to clean up its rights record. Many alleged abuses occur in southeast Turkey where security forces and Kurdish rebels are locked in a bitter conflict that has cost 21,000 lives.
Turkish foreign ministry spokesmen were not immediately available to comment on the report.

The group cited the case of Mahmut Sakar, a lawyer and human rights activist in the southeast, who it said has been charged under the anti-terrorism law for "separatist propaganda" in a statement he gave to the European Commission on Human Rights.
